subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting gain restart-aware or external watchdog surfacing for jobs that start but never record success or failure while the Gateway is memory-starved?
rationale: Current failure alerts run through the same Gateway process, and changing that behavior affects operator expectations, notification noise, and ownership between cron recovery and broader health monitoring.

options.title: Add restart-aware surfacing after memory proof
options.body: Keep #87109 open for a focused design that reports interrupted cron runs after restart once a current-main macOS memory soak identifies the remaining leak state.

options.title: Track only under broad memory leak work
options.body: Move the cron alert concern under the broad Gateway RSS/OOM tracker and close this issue only after maintainers accept losing the separate cron-specific context.

options.title: Design an external watchdog
options.body: Create a product-owned watchdog or health-check path outside the Gateway process, accepting the larger surface area and notification-policy work.

recommendation.title: Add restart-aware surfacing after memory proof
recommendation.body: Keep #87109 open for a focused design that reports interrupted cron runs after restart once a current-main macOS memory soak identifies the remaining leak state.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the clearest recent merge/review connection to the memory-core partial fix that most directly overlaps the issue's suspected trigger path.
